tb21_profile.skill: Drive the openssl CLI to produce a specified X.509 artifact set: a 2048-bit RSA key with 600 permissions, a self-signed certificate with given O/CN and a 365-day validity, a combined key+cert PEM, plus extraction of subject, validity dates and SHA-256 fingerprint, and a Python script that loads the certificate and prints CN and expiry
tb21_profile.domain: TLS/PKI and the OpenSSL toolchain: openssl req/x509/rsa, PEM encoding, X.509 subject fields, certificate fingerprints, Unix file permissions, Python cryptography/pyOpenSSL
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-from-spec / configure: produce several exactly-named artifacts with pinned contents, permissions and formats, then self-verify them

PublicBlob can no longer be constructed; parsing and constructing serialized public-key blobs, the analogue of loading a PEM.

Key-exchange hash computation is wrong; getting a cryptographic digest exactly right, as the SHA-256 fingerprint must be.
parse_date raises on valid input; ISO-8601 date handling, which the YYYY-MM-DD validity and expiry output depends on.
HostKeys lookups stopped working; key-store access semantics in the same crypto library family.
Date parser silently returns None across multiple formats; parsing OpenSSL's date output into a normalised form is the same hazard.
Missing date formatter method; rendering a parsed date as YYYY-MM-DD, the output side of the expiry requirement.
OAuth1 signature verification fails after a refactor; verifying a cryptographic signature correctly, different protocol.

notes: Terminal-Lego-15k clearly beats the old pool here: it holds a dense cluster of openssl self-signed-certificate tasks (RSA 2048 / 365 days / CN, non-interactive -subj, SAN entries, basicConstraints, PKCS#12 bundling) that are mostly 'strong'-verified, and five of them make the final ten. CalibForge contributes the operational half — self-signed cert generation wired into a real HTTPS listener, and CA key permission hardening — also strongly verified. TMax remains competitive with two near-exact generation tasks. The one requirement nothing graded covers well is verification.txt (subject + validity dates + SHA-256 fingerprint written to a report): the only tasks that demand exactly that are in Recursive-Task-Synthesis, which ships no verifier, so I ranked them 1-2 in its per_source list and left them out of the final ten; if the merge wants coverage of that sub-skill, rts_task_06680955a6ae8a8fd821bfea and rts_task_14bd701b9a24f0444c8bbc6a are the candidates to reconsider. SWE-Rebench is unusually strong for a SWE corpus on this task because pyca/cryptography is in it — same library, same X.509 objects — so pyca__cryptography-11201 earns a final-ten slot despite losing on task_form. TerminalWorld is respectable here (key generation with exact PEM paths and file modes) but has no self-signed-certificate-from-spec task.
